questions.stem: A light microscope has a maximum resolution of approximately 200 nm. What does this mean in practice?

options.text: It produces images that are always 200 nm across
It can magnify objects up to 200 nm in size
It cannot distinguish between two objects that are closer together than 200 nm
It can only view objects that are exactly 200 nm wide

questions.explanation: A resolution of 200 nm means the microscope cannot distinguish between two separate points that are closer than 200 nm apart. They would appear as a single blurred point, which is why electron microscopes are needed to see very fine details.
